content.comment_body: Hello, I set up a [product_name] webserver, and it works reliably until there's a power cut. Whenever the power goes out, all values entered through the webserver are erased and have to be entered again. I want these values to be stored persistently. In the attached image, you can see where I enter the values in the block marked in red. Another image shows my [product_name] program and how I'm using that value.

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. The VM memory in the [product_name] isn't protected against power loss. Setpoints should be stored in a parameter of an arithmetic function, rather than as a network input. If values from a remote device (like the webserver) are written to this parameter, the [product_name] saves them in flash memory. To make this work, transfer the value to this parameter using parameter-VM-mapping: go to Tools > Parameter-VM-Mapping.

analysis.insight_summary: Users have noticed that the [product_name] webserver removes all user-entered values after a power interruption, which leads to inconvenience and extra manual effort. There's a lack of clarity about which types of data are automatically retained by the system and which require extra configuration for persistence. Confusion stems from unclear processes for ensuring data retention.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that all values they input or change using the [product_name] webserver will be automatically saved and preserved after power outages, with no need for repeated manual entry.
